title: A Predator That Protects Its Prey's Rivals

scenes.tts: Ecologists in the early nineteen sixties mostly described who lived where, and who ate whom. Then Robert Paine kept one species of sea star off a patch of rocky shore. At Mukkaw Bay, Washington, he began doing just that. By his nineteen sixty six report, the patch held eight species instead of fifteen. Taking a predator away had made the community poorer. How can a species that eats others keep more of them around?

At Mukkaw Bay, Washington, he began doing just that. By his 1966 report, the patch held 8 species instead of 15. Taking a predator away had made the community poorer. How can a species that eats others keep more of them around?
scenes.visual: Two empty patch boxes with question marks; a patch of 15 species dots drops to 8 and the question stays.
scenes.narration: Ecologists in the early 1960s mostly described who lived where, and who ate whom. Then Robert Paine kept one species of sea star off a patch of rocky shore. At Mukkaw Bay, Washington, he began doing just that. By his 1966 report, the patch held 8 species instead of 15. Taking a predator away had made the community poorer. How can a species that eats others keep more of them around?

scenes.tts: The sea star was Pisaster ochraceus. It ate mussels, barnacles, chitons, limpets and snails. Paine wanted to know what would happen if one member of the community were taken out. He kept Pisaster out of one patch of shore. He left an adjacent stretch alone as a control. Then he surveyed both along line transects. The test was simple: remove a species, then measure the community.
scenes.visual: Star with arrows to five prey chips; chips clear to a control box (star inside) and a removal box (star fenced out); dashed transect lines cross both.
scenes.narration: The sea star was Pisaster ochraceus. It ate mussels, barnacles, chitons, limpets and snails. Paine wanted to know what would happen if one member of the community were taken out. He kept Pisaster out of one patch of shore. He left an adjacent stretch alone as a control. Then he surveyed both along line transects. The test was simple: remove a species, then measure the community.

scenes.tts: Why would the shore change? The mechanism was competition for space. On a rocky shore, space is a limiting resource. It is as limiting as light in a forest. Mussels are strong competitors for rock. With Pisaster eating them, space kept opening for weaker competitors.
scenes.visual: Rock patch with a row of mussels and rows of other species; the star eats a mussel, a gap opens labelled space, a weaker competitor grows into it.
scenes.narration: Why would the shore change? The mechanism was competition for space. On a rocky shore, space is a limiting resource. It is as limiting as light in a forest. Mussels are strong competitors for rock. With Pisaster eating them, space kept opening for weaker competitors.

scenes.tts: Now take the sea star away. Without Pisaster, the mussels spread over the rock. They won the competition for space. The weaker competitors lost their footing. The patch lost species.
scenes.visual: Star fenced out with a red cross; mussel blobs grow across the rock while seven of the other-species dots shrink away.
scenes.narration: Now take the sea star away. Without Pisaster, the mussels spread over the rock. They won the competition for space. The weaker competitors lost their footing. The patch lost species.

scenes.tts: Count the species. In the removal patch, richness fell from fifteen species to eight. The control did not lose species in the same way. So the sea star did not help the shore by eating species that harmed the others. It raised richness by freeing space. This was a strong local experiment, with one removal patch and one control.

scenes.visual: Removal rock shrinks left with 15 to 8 counter; control box right; a crossed-out harm-the-others arrow; a one-patch-one-control note.

So the sea star did not help the shore by eating species that harmed the others. It raised richness by freeing space. This was a strong local experiment, with one removal patch and one control.

scenes.tts: Ecologists call this keystone predation. A consumer that prefers to eat a strong competitor indirectly benefits the weaker ones. A keystone species has an effect on its community that is large relative to its abundance. The most common species is not a keystone by default. Keep the rule: judge a species by its effect, not by its numbers.
